contract.reader: A programmer who knows C and basic digital logic but has no embedded experience, starting the Embedded and Real-Time Systems series
contract.problem: Understanding what is inside a microcontroller, how firmware reaches it, and what real-time means precisely enough to reason about deadlines
contract.outcome: Use the timing vocabulary (release, deadline, response time, latency, jitter; hard, firm, soft); read a memory map and drive registers through volatile pointers; explain startup from reset to main; compute timer periods, PWM resolution and ADC step size; see why a superloop couples latencies
contract.contribution: One path from the definition of real time to the hardware that makes timing predictable, with every number worked, a runnable host-side GPIO model and exercises with answers; sets the vocabulary of the whole series
contract.evidence: Worked arithmetic; a C GPIO model and a Python timer-setting search with real output; Arm DDI 0403E.e, ISO/IEC 9899:2011, Kopetz (2011), Lee and Seshia (2017), White (2011), Yiu (2014)
contract.limitations: Generic Cortex-M with invented register layouts; interrupts, DMA, buses, scheduling and measurement left to later entries

findings.location: Section 3.2 second bullet, GPIO program, Section 3.3, Section 5.1 script, Exercise 3 (1280 and 360 px, light and dark)
findings.problem: Code-font ligatures draw |= as a single turnstile glyph, != as ≠, == as a long bar, -> as an arrow and <= as ≤, so the sentence that teaches the C bit operators shows symbols that are not C
findings.whyItMatters: The reader is new to register manipulation and Exercise 3 asks them to read code; anyone copying by hand or searching gets operators that do not exist in C
findings.action: Disable ligatures for code site-wide (font-variant-ligatures: none on .prose code and .prose pre in prose.css)
findings.acceptance: On new captures |=, !=, == and -> appear as two separate characters in Section 3.2, Section 3.3 and Exercise 3 at 1280 and 360 px
findings.resolution: live captures of 7e20c2c (run 40085671258) after PR #57: code shows |= -> != as typed characters; desktop-light-10

findings.problem: Peripherals and Pins boxes are cut at the right edge with no scroll cue; the figure has no caption
findings.whyItMatters: The diagram's point (peripherals reach the pins) is the half a phone reader does not see
findings.action: Top-to-bottom layout or the site-level scroll cue for wide figures, and a one-sentence caption
findings.acceptance: At 360 px all five boxes are visible or a cue shows the figure scrolls; the figure has a caption

findings.location: Section 3.4 table of sections; Section 3.1 memory-map table (360 px)
findings.problem: The Lives at run time in column is entirely behind the table scroll at 360 px; Typical contents of the memory map is cut
findings.whyItMatters: The run-time location is the point of the table and Exercise 5 depends on it
findings.action: Merge the last two columns (stored -> at run time) or shorten cells so the table fits at 360 px
findings.acceptance: At 360 px the run-time location of every section is visible without scrolling the table

findings.location: Sections 5.1 and 5.3, Conventions, Sections 1.2 and 5.2 (1280 and 360 px)
findings.problem: Grouped numbers and number-unit pairs break across lines (48 / 000, 20.83 / ns, 48 / MHz); a period and a comma after inline math wrap alone
findings.whyItMatters: Polish; a split 48 000 reads as two numbers
findings.action: Non-breaking spaces in digit groups and between number and unit; keep punctuation attached to inline math
findings.acceptance: None of the listed splits appears on new captures at 1280 or 360 px
